text: **THE RELOCATION IS EFFECTED AT THE RESOLVER; NO TEXT SWEEP DECIDES WHAT MOVES.** After WP-01 exactly one function resolves a canon path and every reader AND writer goes through it -- checked by pointing that one function at a different directory and requiring every canon read and write to follow with no other edit. **`thread_dir()` MUST STILL RESOLVE `intent/st/<ID>/` AFTERWARDS**, because `info.md` (:577) and `acceptance.md` (:591) hang off it and the views do not move; moving `thread_dir()` wholesale would satisfy AC-01.1's letter -- `intent/st/` holds no `thread.json` -- while emptying `intent/st/` entirely. **THE CRITERION IS THE DISCRIMINATION AND NOT A COUNT.** ic re-measured their own 3-of-17 at `c758af96` and WITHDREW it: the probe's reach was one directory of 41 files against a repo-wide concern, and there is no honest single denominator. **A MECHANICAL SWEEP IS REFUTED BY CONSTRUCTION, AND TWO SINGLE-LINE FIXTURES PROVE IT IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS.** **(a) The matched text must not change and the breaking text does not match** -- `gen_register.sh:256` is one table row whose matching half describes what **v2** did and is TRUE, while the half asserting where **v3** canon lives is the half that breaks and **contains no `intent/st/` at all.** A sweep rewrites a true statement about v2 into a falsehood and leaves the real breakage untouched (ic). **(b) The file is in the hit list for the wrong lines** -- `intentsvcs/src/project.rs` carries the literal at **:485 (a doc comment)** and **:854 (a test)** and at NEITHER line that resolves it: `st_dir()` :482 is `self.intent_dir().join("st")` and `thread_json` :492 is `thread_dir(id).join("thread.json")`. A literal-driven sweep edits the comment, **REPORTS THE FILE HANDLED**, and leaves the resolver at v2 (vc). **AND THE CAREFUL PROBE UNDER-REACHES TOO.** vc's narrowed probe for `intent/st/...thread.json` returned 23 files and **did not contain `intentsvcs/src/export.rs:386`, `format!("st/{}/thread.json", thread.id)`** -- the line writing the canon path INTO THE COMMITTED EXTRACT, which under D34 is the artefact that travels. **cc found that line by BUILDING the relocation, not by grepping for it**, and the Highlander fix fell out: the exporter spelled the path independently while every reader resolved `Project::thread_json`, and its neighbouring comment records the issue arm having ALREADY shipped that bug (`issues/46.json` written where readers opened `issues/0046.json`). **The resolver-driven change reached what no text probe did.** Canon's shape is also FLAT -- `.canon/st/<ID>.json`, not `<ID>/thread.json` -- so a prefix sweep yields **the right prefix with the wrong structure, which reads as a correct migration.** Pinned at `6ee99149`. **AND THE HALF-MIGRATED SITES SPLIT INTO TWO KINDS, WHICH IS THE CLASSIFIER THE LIVE MOVE NEEDS BEFORE IT RUNS, NOT AFTER** (cc 2026-08-19, from a case that went their way): `literal_stdout_parity.rs` had its WRITE repointed to `.canon/st/ST0001.json` while its `create_dir_all` still made `intent/st/ST0001` -- **it failed LOUDLY with `NotFound`.** ic's `${var#pat}` case is the same shape and fails SILENTLY: the half-migrated extraction still returns `ST0056.json` and nothing complains. **THE DISCRIMINATOR IS WHETHER THE UNMIGRATED END CAN STILL PRODUCE A VALUE.** An end that yields a plausible value hides the break; an end that yields nothing announces it. **A missing directory is not a plausible wrong answer -- a wrongly-derived filename is.** **SO A TWO-ENDED SITE IS NOT UNIFORMLY RISKY AND MUST NOT BE TREATED AS SUCH: the sites whose unmigrated end still produces a value are the ones that need a DRIVEN test, and the ones that cannot may rely on their own failure.** Classifying them costs less than driving all of them and strictly less than missing one. **THIS REFINES _a migrator must not do half of a two-ended migration_ from a maxim into a testable property**, and it matters here because **the live move of 57 + 40 files happens ONCE** -- a silent half-migration inside it is discovered by a reader months later, not by the run.
